{"action":"write_file","content":"# Implementation Plan: BatchWriter (batch transactions) for tinydb

**Branch**: `001-transactions` | **Date**: 2026-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-transactions/spec.md`

## Summary

Add `tinydb.journal.BatchWriter(db)` — an additive wrapper around a supplied
`TinyDB` instance that applies batches of `insert`/`remove` operations against
the **default table only**, atomically (R01-R03). Approach (from
[research.md](research.md)): snapshot the complete database state at the storage
level (`db.storage.read()`, deep-copied) before the batch; apply operations
sequentially using the existing public `Table.insert` / `Table.remove` APIs;
on any `ValueError` (malformed op, unknown op, missing doc_id), restore the
snapshot via `db.storage.write(...)` and reset the table's `_next_id` counter,
then re-raise. Deep-copy insert payloads so caller data never aliases stored
data. No changes to existing tinydb modules or upstream tests.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.12 (`/usr/local/bin/python`)

**Primary Dependencies**: none new — stdlib `copy.deepcopy` and the existing
`tinydb` package (`TinyDB`, `Table`, `Storage` ABC) only

**Storage**: whatever storage the supplied `TinyDB` uses (validated against
`MemoryStorage`; `JSONStorage` works identically because the seam is the
`Storage` ABC's `read`/`write`)

**Testing**: pytest (`pytest.ini` present); new project tests in
`tests/test_journal.py`; public acceptance via `acceptance_public.py`
(unmodified); upstream `tests/` must stay green (unmodified)

**Target Platform**: CPython 3.12 on Linux (repo CI environment)

**Project Type**: library (single package `tinydb/`)

**Performance Goals**: N/A for this milestone — correctness/atomicity only;
batch size is unbounded but each op is O(1) table lookups plus the existing
per-op storage read/write cost (no new complexity introduced)

**Constraints**: additive module only (`tinydb/journal.py`); no changes to
`tinydb/database.py`, `tinydb/table.py`, `tinydb/storages.py`, or any upstream
test; default table only; single-threaded `apply` semantics

**Scale/Scope**: one new module (~100-150 lines), one new test file, one
contract artifact

## Constitution Check

*Gates determined based on `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (ratified
2026-02-16, v1.0.0). Evaluated 2026-10-19.*

- **I. TEST-DRIVEN DEVELOPMENT (MANDATORY)** — PASS. Plan mandates
  `tests/test_journal.py` covering every FR (FR-001..FR-009) and every spec
  Edge Case before/alongside implementation; `acceptance_public.py` is the
  authoritative public gate and must pass unmodified.
- **II. MINIMAL DIFF (MANDATORY)** — PASS. The change is one new file
  (`tinydb/journal.py`) plus one new test file. No existing source file is
  modified; no refactoring, no new dependencies, no config changes. The
  wrapper reuses `Table.insert`/`Table.remove` instead of duplicating logic.
- **III. NO FUTURE-PROOFING (MANDATORY)** — PASS. No update ops, no
  multi-table support, no journal-to-disk, no locking — all explicitly out of
  scope for Milestone 1 (see spec Assumptions and contract Out of Scope).
- **IV. SIMPLICITY (MANDATORY)** — PASS. Chosen design is the smallest
  mechanism that satisfies R01-R03: storage-level snapshot/restore + existing
  table APIs. Alternatives (transactional storage, Table subclassing, per-op
  undo log) were evaluated and rejected in research.md R1/R6 as larger
  mechanisms for the same outcome.

**Gate result: PASS — no violations; Complexity Tracking not required.**

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-transactions/
├── plan.md              # This file ($speckit-plan command output)
├── research.md          # Phase 0 output ($speckit-plan command)
├── data-model.md        # Phase 1 output ($speckit-plan command)
├── quickstart.md        # Phase 1 output ($speckit-plan command)
├── contracts/           # Phase 1 output ($speckit-plan command)
│   └── batchwriter.md   # Public contract for tinydb.journal.BatchWriter
├── checklists/
│   └── requirements.md  # Specify-phase quality checklist
└── tasks.md             # Phase 2 output ($speckit-tasks command - NOT created by $speckit-plan)
```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
tinydb/
├── database.py        # UNCHANGED (TinyDB, table registry)
├── table.py           # UNCHANGED (Table.insert/remove/_read_table/_update_table)
├── storages.py        # UNCHANGED (Storage ABC, MemoryStorage, JSONStorage)
└── journal.py         # NEW — BatchWriter (this feature)

tests/
└── test_journal.py    # NEW — project tests for BatchWriter (additive)

acceptance_public.py   # UNCHANGED — public acceptance suite (authoritative)
```

**Structure Decision**: Single-project layout (existing `tinydb/` package +
`tests/`). The feature is one additive module inside the existing package —
no new directories, no new subpackages. Rationale: Principle II (minimal
diff) and the requirement "Implementation source: tinydb/journal.py".

## Complexity Tracking

> No Constitution violations; section intentionally empty.

## Post-Design Re-Check (Phase 1)

Re-evaluated all four principles after producing `research.md`,
`data-model.md`, `contracts/batchwriter.md`, and `quickstart.md`:

- **TDD**: quickstart S1-S9 enumerate the testable behaviors; tasks phase must
  map each to a test in `tests/test_journal.py` first. PASS.
- **Minimal diff**: design still touches exactly one new source file + one new
  test file; the only internal (private) access is `table._next_id = None` on
  rollback (single line, justified in research.md R6 — no public API can reset
  the non-persisted ID counter). PASS.
- **No future-proofing**: no speculative parameters, flags, or hooks in the
  contract. PASS.
- **Simplicity**: snapshot/restore at the storage seam is the minimal atomicity
  mechanism; validation is a flat per-op check. PASS.

**Gate result after Phase 1: PASS.**
